message.content:
Based on my search, here's what you should know about treating a cold:

## Important Facts First

**There is no cure for the common cold.** Colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics won't help. Most colds get better on their own within 7-10 days.

## Over-the-Counter Medicines for Symptom Relief

While these won't cure your cold, they can help you feel more comfortable:

### For Pain, Fever, and Aches
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** – relieves headaches, sore throat, and reduces fever
- **Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)** – helps with aches, pains, and inflammation
- Avoid aspirin in children and teenagers due to risk of Reye's syndrome

### For Nasal Congestion (Stuffy Nose)
- **Decongestants** like **pseudoephedrine (Sudafed)** – shrinks swollen blood vessels in your nose
- **Decongestant nasal sprays** like **oxymetazoline (Afrin)** – work quickly but **do not use for more than 3-5 days** to avoid "rebound" congestion
- Note: The FDA has proposed removing **oral phenylephrine** as an effective decongestant ingredient, though products containing it are still safe to take

### For Runny Nose and Sneezing
- **Antihistamines** (like Benadryl, Chlor-Trimeton) – may help somewhat, though research shows they're not very effective for cold symptoms on their own; they work better when combined with a decongestant
- First-generation antihistamines can cause drowsiness

### For Cough
- **Dextromethorphan** – cough suppressant for when cough interferes with sleep
- **Honey** – effective for cough relief in adults and children over 1 year old (never give honey to infants under 1)
- Note: Coughing helps clear mucus, so suppressing it isn't always necessary

## Non-Drug Remedies That Help

- **Rest** – get plenty of sleep
- **Stay hydrated** – water, juice, warm broth, warm lemon water
- **Warm liquids** – chicken soup, tea, warm apple juice can soothe sore throat and loosen congestion
- **Saline nasal spray or drops** – keep nasal passages moist
- **Humidifier or cool-mist vaporizer** – helps with stuffiness and coughing
- **Saltwater gargle** – ¼ to ½ teaspoon salt in warm water for sore throat
- **Throat lozenges or cough drops** – for adults and children over 4

## Important Warnings

- **Children under 6:** OTC cough/cold medicines are generally **not recommended** and can cause serious side effects
- **Children under 4:** Should not take OTC cold medicines containing antihistamines or decongestants
- **Read labels carefully** – many combination products contain multiple active ingredients; avoid taking duplicate ingredients (especially acetaminophen) to prevent overdose
- **Check with your doctor or pharmacist** if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid problems, diabetes, prostate problems, or take prescription medications

## When to See a Doctor

- Trouble breathing or fast breathing
- Dehydration
- Fever lasting more than 4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Symptoms that improve then worsen
- Chronic medical conditions that get worse

---

**Always consult with your healthcare provider or pharmacist** before taking any medication, especially if you have existing health conditions or take other medications.

Sources:
1. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
2. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
3. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/otc-cold-medicines
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/understanding-common-cold-treatment
